finding: 74 playbook scenarios across the five admitted hubs carry typed gold: 64 concrete modes, 2 defer, 8 UNKNOWN; sk-code contributes only 1.

compiledRoute returns qualified-id targets only; checking expected_leaf_resources requires the live qualifiedIdToLeaf bridge over leaf-manifest.json/mode-registry.json; every dependency is live. Mode-granular must-include, not task-scoped assembly.
Compiled emits route/clarify/defer/reject (canary histogram 50/3/7/7) while gold vocabulary is concrete modes/defer/UNKNOWN; the checker must define non-route mapping itself.

2 defer scenarios; pass = no route; over-detection and silent-default must both fail; excluding defer is worse than including but a degenerate always-defer engine still fails the 64 concrete scenarios.

19 holdout (mcp-tooling 7, cli 2, sk-doc 10), 2 negative, 8 UNKNOWN; holdout must count in the verdict while the fitted-vs-holdout gap is reported; negative is a suppression assertion; UNKNOWN maps to empty expected set.
Per-hub canary fixtures (67 cases) validate the engine's own contract but are compiled expectations, not legacy-authored gold; they supplement defer/reject coverage only.
A gold-only checker has one observation: it is stricter against gold but blind to legacy drift; a shared legacy/gold divergence that Lane C scored as parity becomes a compiled-only failure.
